data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["General lines in a plane can be placed to ensure no three intersect at the same point, maximizing regions.","Cutting a pizza imposes a circular boundary, whereas plane division is infinite.","The constraint of passing through the exact center forces all cuts to be concurrent, which is a special case of plane division."],"overturn_conditions":["A cut passing through the center is shown to be able to intersect previous cuts at distinct points (impossible for straight lines through a single point).","The definition of 'pieces' includes unbounded outer regions."],"shared_structure":["Topological division of a 2D plane by 1D curves.","The formula for the maximum number of regions formed by n lines in a plane is (n^2 + n + 2)/2, which assumes no three lines are concurrent.","When lines are concurrent, the number of regions is less than the maximum."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001","SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["For n concurrent lines, the number of regions is 2n.","The constraint of centrality reduces the problem from maximizing plane regions to counting regions formed by concurrent diameters."]},"claim":"The maximum number of pieces produced by 4 straight cuts through the center of a pizza is 8.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The cuts do not all pass through the exact center, allowing for distinct intersection points.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The cuts are not straight lines.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The pieces are not counted by the standard topological definition of distinct bounded areas.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Any straight line passing through the center of a circle is a diameter and bisects the circle into 2 halves. Since all 4 cuts pass through the exact center, they all intersect at a single point. Therefore, the k-th cut intersects exactly k-1 previous cuts at that single point (not k-1 distinct points). A line passing through a region boundary at a point where m other lines already cross does not pass through m+1 distinct regions, but rather splits exactly m+1 regions (in this case, exactly k regions). With all lines concurrent, the k-th cut splits exactly k regions. The total number of pieces is 1 + sum(k for k=1 to 4) = 1 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 11. Wait, correction: if all cuts pass through the center, they all intersect each other at exactly 1 point. The k-th cut intersects the previous k-1 cuts at 1 single point, thus it crosses k-1 distinct lines but only enters 1 new region on each side. The k-th cut splits exactly 2 regions (one on each side of the center), adding 2 pieces per cut. Total pieces = 2 + 2*3 = 8.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
